chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: There is no manumission for the believer after death.
And no bequest (testamentary gift) after death.
ai.seo_question: Does manumission or bequest take effect automatically after a person's death in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq’s (a) clarification that manumission is an immediate act requiring the owner's life, distinguishing it from the deferred distribution of inheritance, while bequests (*nasiha*) are limited to one-third of the estate and must precede death. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential distinction between the fluidity of personal acts during life and the fixed, divinely mandated shares of heirs that take precedence once the soul departs.
